title: Introduce regional cooldown (snooze) and circuit safety net for transient SLO spikes
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds a regional cooldown snooze window and soft circuit safety net to reduce oscillation during short-lived SLO spikes. No config changes required by default; ops can tune via runtime flags.
body:
Summary: Introduces a short-lived regional 'cooldown' (aka snooze) window that suppresses aggressive eviction/rejoin cycles and pairs it with a circuit safety net that temporarily widens SLO thresholds for tenants during transit spikes. This change is intended to reduce cascade failures and oscillation when regions experience short-lived load/saturation bursts.

Motivation: We've observed repeated thrashing where the eviction/failover logic and circuit reopen logic tugged systems back and forth during transient spikes (see SUP-4821). Two correlated problems: (1) rapid tenant evictions followed by immediate re-joins causing KV-coherence churn and elevation of backend latency, (2) circuit state flips that force broad fallback and subsequent noisy restores.

Design:
- Regional cooldown (snooze): when a region hits an SLO breach threshold, instead of immediately starting aggressive per-tenant evictions and rollbacks, we enter a short cooldown window (config default: 45s) where we prefer soft-rate-limiting, localized prefetch throttling, and conservative eviction scoring.
- Circuit safety net: when circuits would normally open for a tenant because of increasing error/latency rates, a transient safety net increases the circuit open threshold and attaches an exponential backoff before hard-open. The safety net is bounded (max 2x threshold, max 90s) and only applies when regional cooldown is active.
- Telemetry/decisions: we emit a new metric region_cooldown_active{region,reason} and per-tenant cooldown_score to help debugging. A debug endpoint in the control plane exposes active cooldown windows for troubleshooting.
- Rollout: gated behind feature flag runtime.alpha.regional_cooldown. Off by default for Dedicated accounts; enabled on host infra for gradual canary.

Checklist:
- [x] Core algorithm implementation (eviction scorer + safety net)
- [x] Unit tests for cooldown transition states
- [x] Integration test simulating short-lived spike and verifying reduced eviction/rejoin cycles
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards (initial grafana panels)
- [x] Runtime flag and ops docs
- [x] Backstop: automatic disable if region metric stream is stale

Commits summary: - c1f6b9f: implement cooldown state machine and compositor - d4a2e11: integrate safety net into circuit policy - a89d77e: add metrics and control-plane debug endpoint - 9b4c002: tests + docs + runtime flag wiring

Files changed (high level): - pkg/runtime/cooldown/state_machine.go (new) - pkg/runtime/circuit/safety_net.go (new) - pkg/eviction/scorer.go (patched: adjust scoring when cooldown active) - controlplane/handlers/debug_cooldown.go (new endpoint) - tests/integration/cooldown_integration_test.go (new) - docs/ops/regional_cooldown.md (ops runbook) - dashboards/cooldown_overview.json (grafana) Note: changes are purposely small in each file; internal logic is conservative and additive.

Testing and CI: - Local unit test coverage added for state transitions and scoring. - Integration test runs in harness simulate a 60s spike and asserts: fewer than 2 evictions per tenant during spike vs 5 in baseline; KV rejoin latency reduced by 30%. - CI: all checks passed after one flakey test re-run (flaky: end-to-end load harness warmup). ci_status: pass

Review conversation (high level): - Carlos Mendez (reviewer): "Great approach. Can we ensure the cooldown window is observable per-tenant and does not hide persistent failures?" - Author (Priya): "Yes — cooldown_score is emitted per-tenant and we have a secondary detector that escalates if the score stays high for 3 windows." - Evelyn Tran (reviewer): "Concern about bounded safety net increasing operator confusion. Add clear ops docs and a kill-switch." - Author: "Added docs + runtime flag and a control-plane kill-switch endpoint; included in release notes." - Daniel Kim: "Do we need a migration path for Dedicated clusters?" - Author: "Flag disabled by default for Dedicated; ops can enable per-cluster. We'll coordinate with infra rotation." Approvals: - Carlos Mendez approved on 2026-02-23 - Evelyn Tran approved on 2026-02-24

Merge: - Merge method: squash - Merge note: "merged with squash; timed canary to follow for 48h" - Post-merge actions: ops playbook created and channel #infra-cooldown created.

Backwards compatibility and safety: - Default OFF for Dedicated deployments. - Feature flag ensures instant roll-back without binary redeploy. - Additional guard: if control-plane telemetry becomes stale we auto-disable.snooze to avoid masking outages.

Why this is different from previous approaches: Earlier PRs attempted to tune eviction aggressiveness or tweak circuit reboot timers independently which reduced symptoms but not root cause. This PR introduces an explicit temporal decoupling (snooze) combined with a bounded safety net so decisions have short-term tolerance without permanently widening safety margins.

Notes for on-call: - If you see region_cooldown_active continuously fired for >10 minutes, run the disable endpoint and follow runbook in docs/ops/regional_cooldown.md. - For Dedicated customers, check dedicated-config for runtime.alpha.regional_cooldown flag.
